packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/settings_test.go: the ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS refusal case is connect, awaitHookFailure, close, with the same assertion and the same following check that no stream was created.
trickyParts: The two bounds are not one. reconcileWait (30 s) bounds a start that needs no repair. repairedReconcileWait (reconcileWait + 30 s) bounds the reconcile after a repair, because recoverUntilHealthy's backoff reaches maxBackoff = 30 s (internal/bus/recovery.go:309), so a repair that lands just after a failed attempt waits that backoff out before the next attempt runs.

The repair is no longer inside any bounded wait: the test ends awaitHookFailure, restarts the member and starts awaitReconciled, so testnats.Cluster.AwaitReady's 15 s mute restart (nats-server 2.10.29's start race, internal/testnats/cluster.go:138-145) costs the test's own clock and no deadline. That is what round 1's inline comment asked for, and it removes the race the deadline reset had with the bus's backoff.
Plan decision D2 still holds in the new shape: every step runs on the test goroutine, because testnats.Server.Start, Server.Stop and Cluster.AwaitReady call t.Fatal*, which Go forbids off it.
deviations: Round 1's reconcileWait reset after the repair is gone. The reviewer showed it races the bus's backoff: both are 30 s, so a repair past about t0+31 s can fire the fatal just before the bus reconciles. The two-wait split plus repairedReconcileWait replaces it.
discoveredComplexity: awaitReconciled reads the log for one thing only, the failure its own failure message names, so no wait treats a logged failure as a stop condition. awaitHookFailure is the only wait that ends on one, and it leaves the client open: the caller closes it (settings_test.go's refusal case) or repairs and waits again (the new test).
